tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's your Monday September 21st morning briefing.

Macro picture first. Futures are rallying despite a weekend absolutely packed with negative headlines. The S&P is up about 49 points or 65 basis points, the Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Asia was broadly green — Korea up 1.65%, Hong Kong up over 1%, Shanghai up nearly 1%. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with strength in industrials, banks, and tech. Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

So why is the market up given a weekend full of bad news? The answer seems to be one thing: the UN General Assembly runs September 22nd through the 28th in New York, and markets are betting that some diplomatic progress can occur on the Middle East and Iran. Trump said he'd be open to meeting with Iran's president, and critically he reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Oil is sliding about 170 basis points to around $102 a barrel. The bull thesis in a nutshell is this: if oil prices can sustainably drop, nearly every macro problem gets easier — yields come down, inflation cools, margins improve, consumer confidence rebounds. That's the chain reaction the market is pricing in this morning.

Now on the negative side, the geopolitical situation is genuinely alarming. Houthis dramatically escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. Ukraine launched its largest-ever drone strike on Russia hitting a Moscow-area oil refinery. Iran warned of fierce retaliation if the US resumes military action. Motor oil prices are surging in the US with retailers rationing supplies. Oil tanker costs are spiking. The Fed backdrop remains hawkish — Schmid and Kashkari both warned this weekend that inflation is broad-based and not just an oil story. The market is pricing roughly 33 basis points of further hikes at the final two meetings this year, with about 50-50 odds on a hike at the October 28th meeting.

On the company front, the big theme is stress in AI infrastructure. Anthropic's IPO has been delayed, its 2027 revenue projections disappointed, and OpenAI's internal financials show expected negative free cash flow of roughly $280 billion through 2030. Oracle is facing trouble offloading debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center — that project is reportedly hitting a wall with lenders. Big Tech off-balance sheet AI liabilities are up roughly $300 billion in just the last year. These are real structural concerns for the AI trade.

On the positive side, Disney's parks business is outperforming peers by leaning into price promotions and package deals while competitors see traffic declines. Kuehne and Nagel announced a long-term logistics collaboration with Amazon, sending its shares higher in Europe. Novo Nordisk on the other hand disappointed at its analyst day by failing to give investors the granular financial targets they were looking for — shares are sliding. SocGen beat expectations at its investor day, guiding to returns on tangible equity of 13 to 14 percent in 2029 and above 15 percent thereafter.

For the week ahead the big events are US flash PMIs Wednesday, the Trump-Xi summit Thursday, and Meta's Connect conference Wednesday night. Earnings this week include AutoZone Tuesday morning, Cintas, General Mills, and Paychex Wednesday morning, Darden and Sysco Thursday morning, and Costco Thursday night.

Bottom line: today's rally is purely a diplomatic hope trade. If any concrete progress emerges from the UN General Assembly on Middle East tensions, the move could have real legs. If it turns out to be wishful thinking, the underlying macro and geopolitical fundamentals argue for caution. Watch oil and watch the headlines out of New York this week.
